title: Join a shared sacred practice with understanding and consent

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: Shared participation requires a real willing other person and the relevant invitation. Observation can be valuable without being membership or participation in a restricted rite. No ritual requires words one cannot sincerely affirm merely to finish an exercise.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Fictional public remembrance invitation: visitors may sit, listen and offer an optional ordinary recollection; no recording. A separate members’ rite afterward is closed to visitors. Rae welcomes a 10-minute shared secular remembrance with Jo if both prefer that alternative. They may each pass and end early. No actual event or consent exists for the reader.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Choose an allowed route and describe its meaning, permission and participation limits. Identify what a solitary recorded-video study could and could not show.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A host permits observation but asks a visitor to recite a belief they do not hold. Can the visitor remain respectfully silent?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: Observe the public remembrance or use an actually agreed shared fallback; do not enter the closed rite. A solitary video can support study, not shared participation. Later fiction: Jo listens, passes on speaking and leaves before the members’ rite; observation occurred, not membership. Partial: follow conduct without understanding the invitation. Incorrect: claim restricted participation from public access.
criteria: Shared practice is not inferred from solitary viewing
Sincerity and the right to decline remain intact

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: Under that observation invitation, yes. Clarify or leave if the actual conditions change; neither false assent nor pressure on others is needed.
